classification.difficultyReason: Count ordered outcomes for two distinguishable dice, including either order and at least one occurrence.

content.prompt: A green die and a blue die are rolled and the results showing on the top faces are noted. What is the probability of getting:

children.label: a
children.prompt: a 1 on the blue and a 2 on the green

answer.worked:
Write outcomes as (blue, green). There are $6\times6=36$ equally likely outcomes. Only $(1,2)$ is favourable.

$$P(\text{blue 1 and green 2})=\frac{1}{36}.$$

Writing outcomes as (blue, green), the favourable outcomes are $(1,2)$ and $(2,1)$, out of 36 equally likely outcomes.

$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{a 1 and a 2})&=\frac{2}{36}\\P(\text{a 1 and a 2})&=\frac{1}{18}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: a 5 on the green and an odd number on the blue

answer.worked:
Writing outcomes as (blue, green), the favourable outcomes are $(1,5)$, $(3,5)$ and $(5,5)$, out of 36 equally likely outcomes.

$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{green 5 and blue odd})&=\frac{3}{36}\\P(\text{green 5 and blue odd})&=\frac{1}{12}.\end{aligned}$$

answer.short:
$\frac{11}{36}$

Count the row and column containing 5, counting $(5,5)$ once.
answer.worked:
In the two-dice array, 6 outcomes have a blue 5 and 6 have a green 5. The outcome $(5,5)$ belongs to both groups, so there are $6+6-1=11$ favourable outcomes out of 36.

$$P(\text{at least one 5})=\frac{11}{36}.$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: an odd number on the blue and an even number on the green

answer.worked:
The blue die can show 1, 3 or 5. For each of these three rows in the array, the green die can show 2, 4 or 6. There are $3\times3=9$ favourable outcomes out of 36.

$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{blue odd and green even})&=\frac{9}{36}\\P(\text{blue odd and green even})&=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}$$
